history.summary: CONFIRMED but THIN SOURCING (flag): a Chamunda Devi shrine stands at the Rudraprayag confluence of the Alaknanda and Mandakini rivers, near the Rudranath temple at the sangam - a local goddess shrine distinct from the famous Chamunda Devi temples of Kangra (HP), Chamba (HP) and Dewas (MP, seq id chamunda-mata-temple-dewas-tekri). It is a hilltop community shrine of Garhwali deity-worship tradition, surrounded by deodar and pine, with the fierce goddess (slayer of Chanda and Munda) as its deity. Web coverage is sparse and generic - identity, history and hours all need local verification before publication.

name: Chamunda Devi Temple
town_description: Rudraprayag is a Garhwal Himalayan town at the confluence of the Alaknanda and Mandakini rivers, one of the five Panch Prayags and a key halt on the Kedarnath-Badrinath yatra route (~142 km from Rishikesh). It is named after the Rudranath temple at the sangam.

travel.road: Within Rudraprayag town, near the Alaknanda-Mandakini sangam

visitor_information.best_time: March-June and September-November; the yatra season is busiest
